reference.title: Supported audio formats
reference.shortdesc: The audio formats Audacity imports and exports, and when to use each one.

section.p: Audacity imports and exports audio in several formats. Lossless formats keep every sample of the source; lossy formats discard detail to make smaller files. Exported files are named after the project, so podcast-episode-1.aup3 exports as podcast-episode-1.mp3.

section.title: Choosing a format
section.p: Keep a lossless master and export a lossy copy for distribution:

ol.li: Save the project (.aup3) while you are still editing.
Export a WAV or FLAC file as the archive copy.
Export an MP3 or OGG file to share.

section.p: On Linux you can convert between formats afterwards with ffmpeg:

row.entry: Large files, no quality loss. Best for archiving and further editing.
Widely supported, small files. Needs the LAME encoder, bundled since version 2.3.2. Good for sharing and the web.
Open alternative to MP3. Good quality at low bitrates.
Smaller than WAV with no quality loss. Ideal for archiving when space matters.
